nodes.title: Stage 2 Input Guide · Panel Count / 3-Panel Layout / Props
widgets_values:
# Stage 2 input · how many panels, and how to arrange them

1. **Panel Count** — pick 1 to 4.
2. **3-Panel Layout** — only used when you picked 3.
   - `OFF` : one tall panel on the left + two stacked on the right
   - `ON` : one wide panel on top + two side by side below
3. **Pose photo** — used to set the action in Panel 1.
4. **Prop Mode `OFF`** — Panel 2 just displays the prop on its own.
5. **Prop Mode `ON`** — the character actually uses the prop in Panels 1 and 2.
6. Anything else you want goes into **⑧**.

When a prop switch is OFF, its prompt text is removed automatically.

nodes.title: Read First · How To Use This Workflow
widgets_values:
# 🚀 Just follow this order

1. **① LOAD MODELS** — only check that no loader says `MISSING`.
2. **② STAGE 1 INPUT** — drop in one face photo and one outfit photo.
   Cropping is **automatic**; just glance at the two small previews.
3. **③** — only if you want to change body type or styling. (Optional)
4. Press **Queue** → you get **front / side / back** in one sheet → check it in **⑤**.

**Most of the time you are done here. Stage 2 is OFF by default.**

### If you also want a pose / prop sheet
5. Read **⑥**.
6. Put a pose photo in **⑦**, and type into **⑧** if you want.
7. Flip the switch to **ON** and Queue again.

nodes.title: Stage 2 ON/OFF · How To
widgets_values:
# Stage 2 — use it or not?

**Leave it alone and it stays OFF.** Press Queue and you get just the Stage 1 front / side / back sheet. That is enough for most people.

### If you want Stage 2
1. Put a pose photo into **⑦ STAGE 2 INPUT** below.
2. Turn ON only the prop / background switches you actually need.
3. Type anything extra into **⑧**.
4. Flip `Enable STAGE2_SWITCH` below to **ON**, then Queue.

To go back to Stage 1 only, flip the same switch OFF.

> ⚠️ **Stage 2 needs the resolution in ④ set to `1:1 (Square)`.**
> The final 16:9 composite computes its size assuming a square 3-view input.

nodes.title: Panel Request · Translation Instruction Assembly
widgets_values:
You are a deterministic translator for MiniMax H3 image-generation panel instructions.

Turn the user's panel requests into concise English commands. The requests may be written in any language; if they are already English, keep their meaning and only tighten them.
Normalize every panel label to exactly "Panel N:" where N is 1, 2, 3, or 4.
Labels that mean the same thing include: "Panel 3", "panel3", "3rd panel", "third panel".
Preserve all requested expression, pose, framing, camera, prop, action, and composition details.
For a wink, translate explicitly as one eye fully closed and the other eye open.
Output only the translated "Panel N:" lines. Do not explain, summarize, add headings, or invent requests.
If the user input is empty, output nothing.

nodes.title: Stage 1 Prompt · Identity / Body / Wardrobe Role Split
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the adult woman seen in <Picture 1>. Her reference role is IDENTITY ONLY: face, facial geometry, eyes, nose, lips, skin tone, apparent age, and hairstyle including hair length, color, texture and parting.
<Subject 2> is the outfit worn in <Picture 2>. Its reference role is WARDROBE ONLY: garment shapes, cut, length, colors, patterns, materials, footwear and wearable accessories.

summary:
[reference generation] One static character turnaround sheet showing <Subject 1> wearing <Subject 2>, presented as three full-body photographs — front, right side, and back — on a neutral light-grey studio background.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - remains the same person from <Picture 1> in every shot, preserving the exact face, facial geometry, eyes, nose, lips, apparent age and hairstyle. The hairstyle comes exclusively from <Picture 1> and is identical in all three shots: same length, same cut, same parting, same colour, neither tied up nor let down differently between shots. Take only face and hair from <Picture 1>; its clothing, pose, framing, lighting and background do not carry over.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): attribute_transfer - the garments, colors, patterns, materials, footwear and wearable accessories of <Subject 2> are transferred onto the body of <Subject 1>. Nothing else from <Picture 2> transfers: not its wearer's face, hair, hairstyle, hair length, age, gender presentation, shoulder width, muscle mass, torso volume, height, limb thickness, body shape, pose or background. <Picture 2> is a wardrobe swatch only and has no bearing on how <Subject 1>'s hair looks. <Subject 1> wears the outfit; <Subject 1> does not inherit the outfit donor's body.

detailed_description:
The target is one still image, not a video. Photorealistic studio photography on a neutral light-grey seamless background with even soft lighting.
Arrange exactly three equal vertical photographs side by side from left to right, sharing one ground line, one scale, one camera distance and one lighting setup.
FOOTWEAR: read the shoes directly from <Picture 2> and reproduce that exact pair — same shoe type, silhouette, toe shape, sole, heel height, closure, straps or laces, material and colour. Do not assume a style and do not fall back on a familiar one: if <Picture 2> shows flat shoes, sneakers, loafers or boots, keep them flat and closed; if it shows open sandals, keep them open; if the feet are bare, leave them bare. It is the same single pair in all three shots and never changes type between shots — only the camera angle changes.
[Shot 1] Complete full-body front view in a relaxed A-pose, face toward the camera. Both shoes are seen from the front, toes pointing toward the camera.
[Shot 2] Complete full-body strict 90-degree right-side profile view. The shoes are seen edge-on from the side, showing their true side profile — sole line, heel height and closure — with the toe pointing to the side of the frame, not toward the camera.
[Shot 3] Complete full-body back view, photographed from directly behind. The subject faces away from the camera, so both feet point AWAY from the viewer and you see the REAR of the shoes exactly as that shoe type would genuinely look from behind: a closed shoe shows its heel counter and back seam, an open-backed shoe shows the wearer's bare heel resting on the sole. Do not draw toes or the front of the shoes in this shot, do not turn the feet back toward the camera, and never reuse the front view of the shoes for this back view.
The same hairstyle from <Picture 1> is visible in all three shots, only rotated with the head. Show the complete head and both feet in every shot. Keep the face uncovered and do not add a helmet or mask. No extra panel, no action pose, no separate product display, no inset, no duplicate cell, and no text.

The target is one still image, not a video. Photorealistic studio photography on a neutral light-grey seamless background with even soft lighting.
Arrange exactly three equal vertical photographs side by side from left to right, sharing one ground line, one scale, one camera distance and one lighting setup.
FOOTWEAR: read the shoes directly from <Picture 2> and reproduce that exact pair — same shoe type, silhouette, toe shape, sole, heel height, closure, straps or laces, material and colour. Do not assume a style and do not fall back on a familiar one: if <Picture 2> shows flat shoes, sneakers, loafers or boots, keep them flat and closed; if it shows open sandals, keep them open; if the feet are bare, leave them bare. It is the same single pair in all three shots and never changes type between shots — only the camera angle changes.
[Shot 1] Complete full-body front view in a relaxed A-pose, face toward the camera. Both shoes are seen from the front, toes pointing toward the camera.
[Shot 2] Complete full-body strict 90-degree right-side profile view. The shoes are seen edge-on from the side, showing their true side profile — sole line, heel height and closure — with the toe pointing to the side of the frame, not toward the camera.
[Shot 3] Complete full-body back view, photographed from directly behind. The subject faces away from the camera, so both feet point AWAY from the viewer and you see the REAR of the shoes exactly as that shoe type would genuinely look from behind: a closed shoe shows its heel counter and back seam, an open-backed shoe shows the wearer's bare heel resting on the sole. Do not draw toes or the front of the shoes in this shot, do not turn the feet back toward the camera, and never reuse the front view of the shoes for this back view.
The same hairstyle from <Picture 1> is visible in all three shots, only rotated with the head. Show the complete head and both feet in every shot. Keep the face uncovered and do not add a helmet or mask. No extra panel, no action pose, no separate product display, no inset, no duplicate cell, and no text.

# 📦 6 models you download yourself

## ② 4-Step Turbo LoRA · `models/loras/`
[minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/loras/minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors)

## ③ H3 Qwen text encoder · `models/text_encoders/`
[qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors)

## ④ T=1 still-image VAE (for character sheets) · `models/vae/`
[minimax_h3_t1_image_vae_step1597.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Mamad8/MiniMax-H3-Image-VAE/resolve/main/minimax_h3_t1_image_vae_step1597.safetensors)

## ⑤ H3 audio VAE · `models/vae/`
[minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

## ⑥ Gemma image analysis · `models/text_encoders/`
[gemma4_e4b_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Gemma4/resolve/main/text_encoders/gemma4_e4b_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors)

Gemma writes a short description of the pose photo and analyses whichever optional images are switched on. It is **not** used to describe the face or the outfit.

---

## 🤖 These download themselves — do nothing
The models behind the automatic face / outfit cut-out in **② STAGE 1 INPUT**
are **fetched automatically the first time you press Queue.**

- Face cut-out → SAM3
- Outfit cut-out → SegFormer clothes (`models/RMBG/segformer_clothes/`)

Only the first run is slow; after that it is instant.

---
After adding models, refresh the model list. Restart ComfyUI only if they still do not show up.

> This workflow uses the **T=1 still-image VAE**.
> For normal H3 video, use the Video VAE instead.

nodes.title: How To Use · What Each Image Does
widgets_values:
# 📷 You only need 2 photos

- **Left · Face photo** → only the **face and hairstyle** are taken from it.
- **Right · Outfit photo** → only the **clothes and shoes** are taken from it.

### ✂️ Cropping is automatic
The face photo is cut down to the **head only**, and the outfit photo to **clothes and shoes only**.
The face, hair, arms and legs in the outfit photo are removed for you, so **you do NOT need to crop it below the neck first.** A photo with a large visible face is fine.

### 👀 How to check it worked
Look at the two small previews on the right. If you see **only a head** / **only clothes** floating on grey, it worked.
If part of the outfit is missing, toggle the checkboxes (Upper Clothes / Skirt / Pants / Shoes …) on the **Extract Clothes Only** node in the middle.

To change body type or styling, type into **③** — plain English is fine.
e.g. `slim adult female build, narrow shoulders, slender arms and legs`
